:::{#thm-row-null-disjoint}
#### The row space and null space share only the zero vector

For any $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$,

$$
\mathcal{C}(\tp{\matr{A}}) \cap \mathcal{N}(\matr{A}) = \cb{\vzero_n}.
$$

:::

::: proof

Both sets are subspaces,
by @def-column-space and @thm-null-space-subspace,
so both contain $\vzero_n$ (@thm-subspace-zero).

Now take any $\vecf{x}$ in both sets.
Being in the row space means $\vecf{x} = \tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{u}$
for some $\vecf{u} \in \reals^m$ (@def-column-space),
and being in the null space means $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m$
(@def-null-space).
Then

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{x}} \vecf{x}
&= \tp{(\tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{u})}\,\vecf{x}
&& \text{(substitute } \vecf{x} = \tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{u} \text{ in the first factor)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{x}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product, and } \tp{(\tp{\matr{A}})} = \matr{A} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}}\,\vzero_m
&& \text{(substitute } \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m \text{)}
\\
&= 0.
&& \text{(every term of the inner product is } 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

But $\tp{\vecf{x}} \vecf{x} = x_1^2 + \cdots + x_n^2$,
which is $0$ only when every $x_i = 0$.
So $\vecf{x} = \vzero_n$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-row-null-disjoint}
#### The row space and null space in @exm-null-space

For $\matr{A}$ in @exm-column-space,
the row space is $\operatorname{span}\cb{(1, -2, -2)}$
and the null space is $\operatorname{span}\cb{(2, 1, 0), (2, 0, 1)}$
(@exm-null-space).
A vector $c\,(1, -2, -2)$ of the row space is in the null space only if

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\,\paren{c\,(1, -2, -2)}
&= c\,\paren{1 - 2 \cd (-2) - 2 \cd (-2),\; 3\,(1 - 2 \cd (-2) - 2 \cd (-2))}
&& \text{(@exm-null-space's formula for } \matr{A} \vecf{x} \text{)}
\\
&= c\,(9, 27)
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

is $\vzero_2$, that is, only if $c = 0$.
So the two subspaces share only $\vzero_3$.

:::
